title: Getting Paul DeDroit the Chinese Theatre drum job and Fox studio
summary: He brought Paul out, who impressed on Rhapsody in Blue, then the Fox studio job; also the gambling boat.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: So, when, when, when that was, oh, that was, that was before. Paul came on. Uh, they wanted a drummer at the, at the Chinese. And, uh, a versatile drummer because they had put a bottle of show on him, is it? Yeah. And, everybody around town tried for it and couldn't make it. So, I, I heard about the job. And, so, a fellow asked me, he said, do you know any drum? I said, I know it, kid. You could cut that. What do you mean? I don't know, kid, you, the overture was Rhapsody in Blue, you see? Yeah. So, and, and those days the show ran about 10, 12 weeks, see? Same show. So, I get home and there's a letter from Paul. I wonder if they had a job out here. So, I wired him. Come on out. Now, he'd been top, top man around New Orleans and legitimate. Been the orphan for years like he was and all of them. He played the singer theater and all that show music. Yeah. So, he come out. Went down and introduced him to the leader. All right, it was great. So, the guy says, you want to look at the book? So, you want to post on your son with the, you know?

The guy came to me after and said, hey, can this guy pick up that book like that, tell me he knows the show? Don't have to have rehearsal. I said, that's it. You don't have to. All right, now, if the guy follows up the deal, you know? I said, oh, he ain't gonna follow it. So, sure enough. There's an act on the bill called Nothing and Chain. Do a lot of pack balls and moves and the drums got all the cues, you know? Yeah. Paul played the act for 10 years at the offium. So, they opened up, first of all, they opened up with Raps in Blue. Yeah, and the drums are everything. Yeah. And it begins, you see? This leader gets a little. Paul's got the band right in his lap. Other drummers, they're in there but they're weak.
They don't know. They're gonna see what they're gonna do.

Yeah, he's got it right down. And they said, that's it. And that only kid had me. Yeah. And when Nelson and Chain come on, they've been having trouble and trouble and trouble. He kicks the guy in the plat and he whistled. Whooo! Bam! Crash! Singin'. They come up and say, wait, there's something wrong with this band. Look down the corner and there's Paul and he sees him.

And the kid finished out that program and he played all over town. Then, things got slack. So, we finally wind up. I'm broke. Paul's broke. Miller's broke. And, uh, so he gets a job on a gambling boat out in the ocean. Five miles out in the water taxi. Go to work every night.
I know that was it. So, finally Paul gets a call to the studio. He's late. He can't make the boat. And the minute he sits into the studio, that's it. And he's been there ever since Fox.
In the Fox studio. That's good. He's doing fine.
Around twelve, fifteen thousand a year contract.
And those studio musicians make out alright. Yeah.
So, then, little by little the gambling boat went down.
That's the sad part of that. Oh, yeah. Yeah. Oh, they're just old halls out there, you know. Yeah. Had roulette tables and dice games on and stuff.
They had a band for dancing and that was just the gimmick.
